selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends LLDB's DIL expression parser and evaluator to support binary subtraction in addition to addition. It updates additive-expression parsing to accept '-' tokens, maps '-' to a new BinaryOpKind::Sub, adds scalar subtraction evaluation, and wires in a dedicated subtraction entry point with tests for integer and long-long arithmetic.

Behavioral change: Parser now treats '-' as a binary additive operator in DIL expressions.; Binary operator token mapping now recognizes Token::minus as subtraction.; Scalar evaluation now computes l - r for subtraction.; Non-scalar subtraction is rejected with an invalid-operands diagnostic.; Tests exercise subtraction on signed and unsigned integer variables.
Assertion or trace link: No matching LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion terms; No phi-like recipe / non-phi recipe / SmallVector / VPlan trace
Reproducer link: No evidence of clang -O3 crash reproduction; Change is in LLDB expression evaluation, not compiler optimization

They do not touch LoopVectorize, VPlan, VPRecipeBuilder, recipe ordering, or any LLVM vectorizer code implicated by the assertion. Based on the available context, this commit is not a plausible cause of the reported LoopVectorize/VPlan crash.
Causal confidence: 0.98

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/RISCV/vplan-vp-intrinsics-fixed-order-recurrence.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/RISCV/vplan-vp-intrinsics-fixed-order-recurrence.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..43c0367e99a8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/RISCV/vplan-vp-intrinsics-fixed-order-recurrence.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-vectorize -debug-only=loop-vectorize \
+; RUN: -prefer-predicate-over-epilogue=predicate-else-scalar-epilogue \
+; RUN: -mtriple=riscv64 -mattr=+v -riscv-v-vector-bits-max=128 -disable-output < %s 2>&1 | FileCheck --check-prefix=IF-EVL %s
+
+define void @first_order_recurrence(ptr noalias %A, ptr noalias %B, i64 %TC) {
+; IF-EVL: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={1},UF>=1'
+; IF-EVL-NOT: EXPLICIT-VECTOR-LENGTH-BASED-IV-PHI
+;
+; IF-EVL: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={vscale x 1,vscale x 2,vscale x 4},UF={1}' {
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Live-in vp<[[VF:%[0-9]+]]> = VF
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Live-in vp<[[VFUF:%[0-9]+]]> = VF * UF
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Live-in vp<[[VTC:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-trip-count
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Live-in ir<%TC> = original trip-count
+; IF-EVL-EMPTY:
+; IF-EVL: ir-bb<entry>:
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Successor(s): scalar.ph, vector.ph
+; IF-EVL-EMPTY:
+; IF-EVL: vector.ph:
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:  EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[VF32:%[0-9]+]]> = trunc vp<[[VF]]> to i32
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Successor(s): vector loop
+; IF-EVL-EMPTY:
+; IF-EVL: <x1> vector loop: {
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:   vector.body:
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[IV:%[0-9]+]]> = CANONICAL-INDUCTION
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EXPLICIT-VECTOR-LENGTH-BASED-IV-PHI vp<[[EVL_PHI:%[0-9]+]]> = phi ir<0>, vp<[[IV_NEXT:%.+]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     FIRST-ORDER-RECURRENCE-PHI ir<[[FOR_PHI:%.+]]> = phi ir<33>, ir<[[LD:%.+]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[AVL:%.+]]> = phi [ ir<%TC>, vector.ph ], [ vp<[[AVL_NEXT:%.+]]>, vector.body ]
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[PREV_EVL:%.+]]> = phi [ vp<[[VF32]]>, vector.ph ], [ vp<[[EVL:%.+]]>, vector.body ]
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[EVL]]> = EXPLICIT-VECTOR-LENGTH vp<[[AVL]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     vp<[[ST:%[0-9]+]]> = SCALAR-STEPS vp<[[EVL_PHI]]>, ir<1>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     CLONE ir<[[GEP1:%.+]]> = getelementptr inbounds nuw ir<%A>, vp<[[ST]]
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     vp<[[PTR1:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-pointer inbounds nuw ir<[[GEP1]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN ir<[[LD]]> = vp.load vp<[[PTR1]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN-INTRINSIC vp<[[SPLICE:%[0-9]+]]> = call llvm.experimental.vp.splice(ir<[[FOR_PHI]]>, ir<[[LD]]>, ir<-1>, ir<true>, vp<[[PREV_EVL]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>)
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN ir<[[ADD:%.+]]> = add nsw vp<[[SPLICE]]>, ir<[[LD]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     CLONE ir<[[GEP2:%.+]]> = getelementptr inbounds nuw ir<%B>, vp<[[ST]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     vp<[[PTR2:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-pointer inbounds nuw ir<[[GEP2]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN vp.store vp<[[PTR2]]>, ir<[[ADD]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[CAST:%[0-9]+]]> = zext vp<[[EVL]]> to i64
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[IV_NEXT]]> = add vp<[[CAST]]>, vp<[[EVL_PHI]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[AVL_NEXT]]> = sub nuw vp<[[AVL]]>, vp<[[CAST]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[IV_NEXT_EXIT:%.+]]> = add vp<[[IV]]>, vp<[[VFUF]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT branch-on-count  vp<[[IV_NEXT_EXIT]]>, vp<[[VTC]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:   No successors
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: }
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Successor(s): middle.block
+; IF-EVL-EMPTY:
+; IF-EVL: middle.block:
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Successor(s): ir-bb<for.end>
+
+; IF-EVL: Cost of 0 for VF vscale x 4: FIRST-ORDER-RECURRENCE-PHI ir<[[FOR_PHI]]> = phi ir<33>, ir<[[LD]]>
+; IF-EVL: Cost of 4 for VF vscale x 4: WIDEN-INTRINSIC vp<[[SPLICE]]> = call llvm.experimental.vp.splice(ir<[[FOR_PHI]]>, ir<[[LD]]>, ir<-1>, ir<true>, vp<[[PREV_EVL]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>)
+entry:
+  br label %for.body
+
+for.body:
+  %indvars = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %indvars.next, %for.body ]
+  %for1 = phi i32 [ 33, %entry ], [ %0, %for.body ]
+  %arrayidx = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %A, i64 %indvars
+  %0 = load i32, p

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Fix masked_cond expansion.
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit fixes masked_cond expansion in VPlanTransforms by swapping the operands used to build the logical-and recipe. The accompanying LoopVectorize tests update expected select operand ordering in several predicated early-exit and multi-exit cases.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes; predicated-early-exits-interleave.ll; predicated-single-exit.ll; predicated-multiple-exits.ll
Behavioral change: Changes masked_cond lowering from logical-and(value, mask) to logical-and(mask, value).; Updates generated select/check ordering in predicated early-exit and multi-exit vectorization tests.; Affects how VPlan concrete recipes are materialized for masked conditions.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; recipe ordering; phi-like recipe; non-phi recipe
Reproducer link: predicated early-exit and multi-exit vectorization patterns; select ordering changes in LoopVectorize output
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlanTransforms; predicated loop vectorization
Causal explanation: This is directly in the LoopVectorize/VPlan area and changes how concrete recipes are built for masked conditions, which can affect recipe ordering and plan shape. The retrieved evidence does not mention phi-like recipes or the exact assertion, but the subsystem and recipe-construction nature make it plausibly related to a VPlan ordering bug.
Causal confidence: 0.84
Build risk: Core LoopVectorize/VPlan transform change; Multiple regression tests adjusted for emitted IR differences; Recipe operand ordering changed, which can affect downstream plan invariants

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Optimize FindLast of (binop %IV, live-in) by sinking. (#183911)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This VPlanTransforms change extends the "find-last IV" sinking optimization so it can recognize when the expression being sunk is itself derived from a widened induction variable, then rebuilds the select/reduction using the underlying IV and a separately cloned scalar expression. It also changes the middle-block reduction construction to use the vector-region exiting value instead of the previously reduced IV, and updates tests to reflect the new recipe/value ordering and sentinel handling.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::optimizeFindIVReductions; getExpressionIV; vputils::getSCEVExprForVPValue; VPBuilder; VPRecipeBase::getDefiningRecipe; createSelect; createNaryOp; cloneBinOpForScalarIV
Behavioral change: Detects sinkable expressions that are based on an induction variable and substitutes the underlying IV for SCEV analysis.; Rebuilds the find-last select so the phi/backedge value can track the underlying IV directly when sinking is possible.; Uses the vector-region exiting value in the middle-block select/n-ary op instead of the previously reduced IV.; Adds an assertion that the IV-expression classification and the FindLastExpression classification stay consistent.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; phi-like recipe; non-phi recipe; recipe ordering; assert
Reproducer link: crash at -O3; VPlan assertion during vectorizer plan construction; find-last / sinkable expression epilogue cases
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlanTransforms
Causal explanation: This commit is plausibly related because it directly changes VPlan recipe/value construction in LoopVectorize, including select rebuilding and sinking logic that can affect recipe ordering. The added assertion and the new handling of sinkable IV expressions indicate the code was already sensitive to invariants around expression classification and plan construction. However, the retrieved hunks do not mention the exact "Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe" assertion, so the link is indirect rather than proven.
Causal confidence: 0.72
Build risk: Touches high-risk LoopVectorize/VPlan code paths; Adds new assertion in optimization logic; Updates multiple VPlan/LoopVectorize tests, suggesting observable behavior changes; Changes recipe construction order and value plumbing, which can affect SmallVector-backed plan storage and invariant checks

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Support plain CFG plans in the verifier. (#181817)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit relaxes and extends VPlan verifier checks so that plain CFG plans and certain non-dominating MaskedCond-related uses are accepted. It removes a header/latch structural check for plans without a parent region, adds special-case verifier exemptions for MaskedCond definitions and recipes used from exit blocks, and updates LoopVectorize to run several VPlan transforms through verifier-enabled wrappers. The test update records additional VPlan-print-after-all checkpoints around the vectorizer pipeline.
Changed symbols: VPlanVerifier::verifyBlock; VPlanVerifier::verifyVPBasicBlock; VPBlockUtils::isHeader; VPBlockUtils::isLatch; LoopVectorizationPlanner::buildVPlansWithVPRecipes; VPlanTransforms::handleEarlyExits; VPlanTransforms::addMiddleCheck; VPlanTransforms::createLoopRegions
Behavioral change: Removes a verifier rule that required plain CFG VPlans to have a specific header/latch predecessor ordering.; Allows MaskedCond recipes to violate normal dominance expectations because they are expected to be linearized later.; Allows recipes in blocks with MaskedCond to be used from exit blocks even if dominance is not yet satisfied.; Changes LoopVectorize to verify more VPlan transforms during construction, which can surface or prevent ordering issues earlier.
Assertion or trace link: Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe; VPlan recipe ordering; LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion
Reproducer link: Crash occurs during -O3 vectorization on a real input; Issue mentions VPlan plan construction and recipe ordering
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlanVerifier; VPlanTransforms

However, the retrieved hunks do not show any direct change to phi-like recipe insertion or ordering logic, only verifier relaxations and pass-wrapping. That makes it plausible as a related fix or enabling change, but not strong evidence that it directly addresses the specific 'phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe' crash.
Causal confidence: 0.42
Build risk: High-risk path in llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize; Verifier behavior changed, so tests may start failing or newly pass depending on plan shape; Pipeline now runs more transforms under verification, increasing sensitivity to latent VPlan invariants

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Simplify add x, (sub 0, y) -> sub x, y (#187228)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit adds a VPlan simplification that rewrites add x, (sub 0, y) into sub x, y while preserving no-signed-wrap flags when both source operations had them. The change is in VPlanTransforms and is accompanied by LoopVectorize test expectation updates showing the new sub-based form in several vectorization cases.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::simplifyRecipe; VPRecipeWithIRFlags; VPIRFlags; Builder.createSub
Behavioral change: Introduces a new VPlan canonicalization rule that replaces an add of a negated value with a subtraction.; Preserves nsw semantics on the new subtraction when both original operations were nsw.; Can change the shape and ordering of recipes produced during VPlan simplification, potentially affecting downstream recipe sequencing.
Assertion or trace link: Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe; VPlan recipe ordering; phi-like recipe
Reproducer link: Crash happens during LoopVectorize/VPlan construction at -O3; Issue is sensitive to recipe ordering and SmallVector-backed recipe storage

A new rewrite can alter recipe creation and ordering, which is relevant to a verifier complaining about phi-like recipes appearing after non-phi recipes. top_candidates.subject: [LV] Remove IV use restrictions for epilogue vectorization. (#190552)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit removes induction-variable use restrictions for epilogue vectorization in LoopVectorize and updates several LoopVectorize tests to expect new iteration-check and epilogue-vectorization control flow. The functional change broadens when epilogue vectorization is considered legal for loops with induction-variable live-outs, which can alter planner decisions and generated VPlan structure.
Changed symbols: LoopVectorizationPlanner::isCandidateForEpilogueVectorization; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/X86/transform-narrow-interleave-to-widen-memory.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/X86/transform-narrow-interleave-to-widen-memory-live-outs.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/X86/transform-narrow-interleave-to-widen-memory-epilogue-vec.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/X86/iv-live-outs.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/optimal-epilog-vectorization-liveout.ll
Behavioral change: Removes checks that rejected epilogue vectorization when induction variables had uses outside the loop.; Allows loops with IV live-outs to proceed through epilogue vectorization planning.; Introduces/updates test expectations for additional iteration checks and epilogue-vectorization branches.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; recipe ordering; phi-like recipe; assertion
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O3; real GitHub attachment crash-62b480.cpp; vectorizer plan construction
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize/LoopVectorize.cpp
Causal explanation: This is directly in the reported subsystem and changes legality/planning for epilogue vectorization, which can affect VPlan construction and recipe ordering. Although the diff does not mention the specific assertion, removing IV-use restrictions plausibly changes the shape of plans involving live-out phis and could expose ordering bugs in VPlan recipe insertion.
Causal confidence: 0.74

Summary: This commit is an NFC cleanup that changes VPWidenPHIRecipe construction to take all incoming values up front instead of constructing with a start value and then appending operands. top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Use MaxRuntimeStep in materializeVectorTC to simplify middle br. (#193067)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends LoopVectorize/VPlan trip-count materialization to account for a maximum possible runtime step on scalable vector targets. It threads an optional MaxRuntimeStep from LoopVectorizationPlanner::executePlan into VPlanTransforms::materializeVectorTripCount, and adds a fast path that reuses the scalar trip count directly when it is a constant divisible by that maximum step. The accompanying test updates remove checks for modulo-based epilogue computation in scalable-vector cases, indicating a change in how vector trip counts and middle-block control flow are formed.
Changed symbols: LoopVectorizationPlanner::executePlan; VPlanTransforms::materializeVectorTripCount; VPlanTransforms::materializeVectorTripCount(VPlan &, VPBasicBlock *, bool, bool, VPValue *, std::optional<uint64_t>); llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/simple_early_exit.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/sve-epilog-vect.ll
Behavioral change: Computes and passes a MaxRuntimeStep derived from max vscale, VF, and UF into VPlan trip-count materialization.; Adds an invariant: if the scalar trip count is a constant divisible by the maximum runtime step, the vector trip count is replaced with the scalar trip count directly.; Removes the need to materialize a urem/sub sequence for some scalable-vector epilog/middle-block cases.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; vector trip count; middle block; scalable VF; phi-like recipe ordering assertion
Reproducer link: Affects -O3 vectorization behavior on scalable-vector AArch64 tests; Changes early-exit and epilog vectorization codegen patterns
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlanTransforms; vectorizer plan construction
Causal explanation: The retrieved hunks are in the exact subsystem named by the issue and alter VPlan construction/materialization, which is high-risk for recipe ordering bugs. However, the visible change is about trip-count simplification for scalable vectors, not directly about phi-like recipe ordering or SmallVector-backed recipe storage. It could indirectly perturb recipe ordering by changing which blocks/recipes are materialized, but the evidence is only indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.42

top_candidates.subject: Revert "[clang] fix matching constrained out-of-line definitions of class specialization member function templates" (#193558)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit is a Clang Sema revert that removes logic for matching constrained out-of-line definitions of class specialization member function templates and associated deduction-guide constraint instantiation handling. The hunks show substantial changes in template argument collection for function templates and deduction guides, including special handling for nested class template specializations and injected template arguments. The visible tests are C++ concepts/out-of-line-definition tests, not LLVM vectorization tests.
Changed symbols: HandleFunctionTemplateDecl; buildAssociatedConstraints; SemaTemplateDeductionGuide; SemaTemplateInstantiate; clang/test/SemaTemplate/concepts-out-of-line-def.cpp; clang/docs/ReleaseNotes.rst
Behavioral change: Removes/backs out template instantiation and constraint-building logic for constrained out-of-line definitions.; Changes how outer template arguments are assembled for deduction-guide constraint substitution.; Adjusts handling of nested class template specializations and injected template arguments during Sema processing.
Assertion or trace link: No matching LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion visible; Clang Sema template matching / constrained out-of-line definitions
Reproducer link: C++ concepts and out-of-line definition tests; Template deduction-guide matching behavior
Pass or subsystem link: Clang Sema; Template instantiation/deduction guide handling
Causal explanation: The issue is a LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion in LLVM, but this commit only touches Clang semantic analysis for templates and deduction guides. There is no evidence in the retrieved hunks that it affects VPlan recipe ordering, LoopVectorize, or vectorizer plan construction. Based on the visible context, it is not a plausible direct cause of the reported LLVM crash.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Different component than the reported crash (Clang Sema vs LLVM vectorizer); No overlap with VPlan/LoopVectorize paths in retrieved hunks; Test changes are unrelated to vectorization

@@ -933,0 +931,42 @@ buildAssociatedConstraints(Sema &SemaRef, FunctionTemplateDecl *F,
+  ArgsForBuildingRC.addOuterTemplateArguments(TemplateArgsForBuildingRC);
+  // For 2), if the underlying deduction guide F is nested in a class template,
+  // we need the entire template argument list, as the constraint AST in the
+  // require-clause of F remains completely uninstantiated.
+  //
+  // For example:
+  //   template <typename T> // depth 0
+  //   struct Outer {
+  //      template <typename U>
+  //      struct Foo { Foo(U); };
+  //
+  //      template <typename U> // depth 1
+  //      requires C<U>
+  //      Foo(U) -> Foo<int>;
+  //   };
+  //   template <typename U>
+  //   using AFoo = Outer<int>::Foo<U>;
+  //
+  // In this scenario, the deduction guide for `Foo` inside `Outer<int>`:
+  //   - The occurrence of U in the require-expression is [depth:1, index:0]
+  //   - The occurrence of U in the function parameter is [depth:0, index:0]
+  //   - The template parameter of U is [depth:0, index:0]
+  //
+  // We add the outer template arguments which is [int] to the multi-level arg
+  // list to ensure that the occurrence U in `C<U>` will be replaced with int
+  // during the substitution.
+  //
+  // NOTE: The underlying deduction guide F is instantiated -- either from an
+  // explicitly-written deduction guide member, or from a constructor.
+  // getInstantiatedFromMemberTemplate() can only handle the former case, so we
+  // check the DeclContext kind.
+  if (F->getLexicalDeclContext()->getDeclKind() ==
+      clang::Decl::ClassTemplateSpecialization) {
+    auto OuterLevelArgs = SemaRef.getTemplateInstantiationArgs(

If the existing declaration's definition location is invalid, the loader skips the duplicate-definition comparison instead of relying on incomplete location data.
Changed symbols: ModuleMapLoader::handleModuleDecl; modulemap::ModuleDecl; ExistingModMapFile; CurrentModMapFile; Existing->DefinitionLoc
Behavioral change: Suppresses duplicate module-definition checks when the existing definition location is unknown.; Preserves conservative behavior by avoiding comparisons that cannot be validated.; Changes module map loading diagnostics/validation, not code generation.
Assertion or trace link: Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe; VPlan; LoopVectorize
Reproducer link: crash at -O3; real GitHub attachment crash-62b480.cpp
Pass or subsystem link: Clang Modules; ModuleMap
Causal explanation: The retrieved hunks are entirely in Clang module-map handling and do not interact with LLVM vectorization, VPlan, or recipe ordering. There is no evidence of relevance to the reported assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.01
Build risk: Frontend module-loading logic change; Diagnostic/validation behavior altered; No overlap with the reported optimizer crash path

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit expands RISCV support for vp.inttoptr and vp.ptrtoint lowering and updates RVV codegen tests to match new instruction selection and vsetvli forms. The visible edits are in RISCV target transform info and RVV codegen checks, with no changes to LoopVectorize, VPlan, or recipe ordering logic.
Changed symbols: RISCVTargetTransformInfo; Intrinsic::vp_inttoptr; llvm/test/CodeGen/RISCV/rvv/vp-inttoptr-ptrtoint.ll; llvm/test/CodeGen/RISCV/rvv/fixed-vectors-inttoptr-ptrtoint.ll
Behavioral change: Adjust target support for vector pointer/int conversion intrinsics on RISC-V.; Change expected codegen patterns for vsetvli/vsetivli and masked vector conversion instructions.; Remove or alter masked forms in test expectations to reflect new lowering behavior.
Assertion or trace link: No VPlan or phi-like recipe assertion appears in the retrieved hunks; No LoopVectorize crash trace is evidenced by the visible changes
Reproducer link: The tests cover RVV inttoptr/ptrtoint code generation, not an -O3 vectorizer crash; The patch concerns backend lowering of intrinsics rather than vectorizer plan construction
Pass or subsystem link: RISCV backend; TargetTransformInfo; CodeGen/RISCV RVV
Causal explanation: Although this commit touches vector-related intrinsics, it is backend-specific RISCV lowering work and test updates. The reported bug is an LLVM LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion about recipe ordering, so the retrieved hunks do not provide evidence that this commit could trigger or fix that issue.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Touches target-specific lowering and codegen tests only; No LoopVectorize/VPlan source or tests are modified; Potentially relevant only if the crash were backend-triggered, which is not supported by the retrieved context

Summary: This commit fixes Flang's inline transfer lowering for unsigned integer types by broadening the type check to accept signless integer or float types. The added test ensures unsigned transfer uses fir.convert and load rather than arith.bitcast or a runtime transfer call. The change is confined to Flang intrinsic lowering and its tests.
Changed symbols: IntrinsicLibrary::genTransfer; mlir::Type::isSignlessIntOrFloat; flang/test/Lower/Intrinsics/transfer-unsigned.f90; trans_test_unsigned
Behavioral change: Allow inline transfer lowering when source and result types are signless integer or float.; Avoid using arith.bitcast for unsigned integer destinations, instead converting the reference type and loading through FIR.; Preserve inline lowering for the unsigned case without falling back to the runtime transfer helper.
Assertion or trace link: No LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion terms are present in the retrieved hunks; No 'Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe' evidence is present
Reproducer link: The test is a Fortran unsigned transfer lowering case, not a Clang C++ -O3 vectorizer crash; The behavior change is about FIR/MLIR lowering semantics, not LLVM vector recipe ordering
Pass or subsystem link: Flang optimizer builder; IntrinsicCall / transfer lowering; HLFIR/FIR lowering
Causal explanation: This is a Flang lowering fix unrelated to LoopVectorize and VPlan. The retrieved hunks show no interaction with LLVM vectorization passes or recipe storage/order, so there is no evidence-backed causal connection to the reported assertion.
